summary: es6-migrator preinstall beacon exfiltrates installer host/user/path to hardcoded IP with DNS-tunnel fallback
details: The package's sole functional content is a preinstall beacon. package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node beacon.js' with no main entry, no library code, and only a stub refuse-publish.js alongside the beacon. On npm install, beacon.js reads os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username and process.cwd() and transmits them, base32-encoded, in custom X-Bug-Bounty-Host / X-Bug-Bounty-User / X-Bug-Bounty-Path headers via a plain-HTTP GET to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://45.76.249.245/beacon/Dl0X4pr0iz3pR1luglaGnut3kCyB_vft/es6-migrator/1.0.0. If the HTTP request fails, the beacon falls back to DNS exfiltration, issuing resolve4/resolve6/resolveTxt lookups with the same identifiers encoded as base32 subdomain labels under three preconfigured *.oob.asm5.net domains, bypassing HTTP egress filtering. The package name mimics a plausible internal ES6 migration utility and the description self-labels the code as a 'controlled dependency-confusion proof', but that framing is author-controlled: any developer or CI job that resolves this public name has host, user and working-directory identifiers shipped to an operator-controlled bare-IP endpoint without consent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
